trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any smart contract or EOA can invoke precompiles. Input data is arbitrary and must be fully validated before processing.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Smart contract or EOA that invoked the BLAKE2F precompile via CALL

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet users provide transaction parameters and replacement requests. While authenticated via signatures, the wallet/provider must validate all input parameters before processing.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: User who initiated the transaction and wants faster confirmation

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can invoke the MODEXP precompile with arbitrary input. The precompile must validate all input lengths and handle edge cases defensively.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Smart contract invoking MODEXP for RSA, primality testing, or cryptographic operations

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Input data to precompiles may be malformed, excessively large, or crafted to exploit edge cases. Robust input validation is mandatory.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Contract providing potentially malformed input data

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block data from network or local production must be validated against consensus rules before determining fork activation. Malformed or malicious blocks could cause incorrect fork transitions.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Block data from network or local production containing block number and timestamp

trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network peers are untrusted by default. Blocks received from peers must pass full validation before acceptance. Malicious peers may send invalid blocks attempting to cause consensus failures.
trusted_external_entities.original_description: Other node sending blocks for validation

security_assumptions: Input length is validated to be exactly 213 bytes before parsing
Final flag value is validated to be 0 or 1
Gas is charged based on rounds parameter before computation
User is authenticated via wallet signature
Gas price increase meets minimum 10% threshold
Only the original transaction sender can request cancellation
Cancel transaction must be self-send with zero value
Length fields are parsed as big-endian uint256
Gas cost scales with computational complexity
Zero modulus case returns zeros without division
Block number and timestamp are validated against consensus rules
Fork activation thresholds are agreed upon by all nodes
Block timestamps cannot be arbitrarily manipulated by validators
Block must pass full validation before acceptance
Fork rules are determined based on block metadata
Invalid blocks are rejected regardless of source peer
